related_questions.question: What is it like to live with someone with anorexia?
related_questions.snippet: Remember that when someone has an eating disorder, they are often protective and private about it. They can feel threatened if someone tells them they need to seek help for it and may lash out in anger or denial. Try not to take it personally and try again later.
related_questions.title: Living With Someone With An Eating Disorder

related_questions.question: Why is anorexia so hard to treat?
related_questions.snippet: Anorexia gets worse the longer it goes untreated, and so do the physical and mental health effects that come with it. Longstanding habits are harder to change. People with anorexia also tend to deny that they have a problem. They might resist treatment or might not stick to their treatment plan long term.
related_questions.title: Anorexia Nervosa: What It Is, Signs & Symptoms, & Treatment

related_questions.question: What is the most effective treatment for eating disorders?
related_questions.snippet: Outpatient cognitive behavioral therapy for bulimia nervosa is the treatment with the strongest evidence. It helps patients normalize their eating behavior and manage thoughts and feelings that perpetuate the disorder. Antidepressants (e.g. fluoxetine) can also be helpful in decreasing urges to binge and vomit.

related_questions.question: How does someone with anorexia feel?
related_questions.snippet: People with anorexia often have common traits, including: low self-esteem, feeling worthless or like you're not good enough. Losing weight can start to feel like a sense of achievement or a way to feel a sense of worth. perfectionism.

answer_box.title: How to help someone with eating disorder - NHS
answer_box.snippet: Give your time, listen to them and try not to give advice or criticise – this can be tough when you do not agree with what they say about themselves and what they eat. Remember, you do not have to know all the answers. Just making sure they know you're there for them is what's important.
